We’re still living with the consequences of that dark day!October 7. The grief didn’t stay behind in Gaza. It followed us. This morning, I lost another one of my cats. She was hit by a car right in front of my home. She’s the eighth out of my nine cats that I’ve lost. This year’s olive harvest has been the most violent in recent memory, with settler attacks on Palestinian farmers reaching a new high. But for Masafer Yatta, this is only the latest escalation in a decades-long campaign by the Israeli state to expel Palestinians from their land by any means necessary. Working in coordination with the army and police, nearby settlers wage a ceaseless battle against the Palestinians living in this area. Professor Ilan Pappé describes what has been happening to Masafer Yatta since the 1970’s as “incremental colonization, ethnic cleansing, and oppression,” and to be here is to see it firsthand. But the people of Masafer Yatta have earned a reputation for themselves for their resistance to state and settler terror. They simply refuse to leave, and the Israelis simply won’t stop trying to force them to. The Nakba never ended. We’re just watching its latest act.
